raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# PR type
- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Document Updates
- [ ] More Models or Datasets Support

# PR information

Related issue: none. This addresses the GSPO + entropy filtering combination documented in [FAQ Q28](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift/blob/484e836d691a52fd8c1723137ee3d64c6e066683/docs/source/Instruction/Frequently-asked-questions.md#L210-L211).

With `importance_sampling_level="sequence"` and `top_entropy_quantile < 1`, the entropy mask removes per-token loss elements, but the remaining elements still depend on every completion logprob through the shared sequence importance ratio. Consequently, low-entropy tokens excluded by the mask can still receive direct policy gradients.

I keep the importance ratio computed from the full completion and reuse the existing GSPO-token gradient expression when an entropy mask is active. Its forward value remains the sequence ratio, so clipping still uses the same sequence-level value; each token's policy loss now differentiates through that token's logprob, allowing the existing entropy mask to select the intended gradient contributions.

The change is limited to the ordinary GRPO and Megatron loss methods: two production files, six added lines and two removed lines. GSPO without entropy filtering keeps its original gradient path. The existing token and sequence-token modes are unchanged, and KL remains outside entropy filtering. For vanilla GSPO with constant per-sequence advantages, the corrected policy gradient is the unfiltered GSPO gradient with the excluded token contributions removed. When token advantages or detached token weights vary, entropy filtering uses the existing GSPO-token gradient semantics explicitly through this branch.

## Experiment results

For two five-token completions with advantages +1 and -1, current policy equal to old policy, `beta=0`, and an entropy mask keeping only the first token of each completion:

| Positive-advantage completion | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selected token's logprob gradient | -0.02 | -0.10 |
| Each excluded token's logprob gradient | -0.02 | 0 |
| Nonzero logprob gradients across both completions | 10/10 | 2/10 |

Both scalar losses are zero because the two advantages cancel. The negative-advantage completion has the opposite gradient signs.

Local validation:

- `python -m pytest ../ms-swift-gspo-entropy-review/test_fix.py -q`: **211 passed**. CPU FP32/FP64 checks cover the imported ordinary loss method and the complete Megatron loss method extracted from source with model/collective substitutes. Cases include off-policy ratios, both clipping directions, unequal completion lengths, empty/fully filtered completions, entropy ties, different retained fractions, unchanged paths, and the unmasked KL contribution.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_align/test_grpo_loss.py -q`: **25 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks passed.
- `python -m pytest ../ms-swift-gspo-entropy-review/test_followup.py -q -k 'not tiny_causal_model_gpu_backward'`: **38 passed**. Follow-up checks cover mixed-sign token advantages, FIPO and dual clipping, off-policy/truncated completion filters, single valid tokens, unchanged REAL behavior, and clipping/entropy/FIPO metrics.
- `python -m pytest ../ms-swift-gspo-entropy-review/test_followup.py -q -k tiny_causal_model_gpu_backward`: **4 passed** on an NVIDIA RTX A1000. A randomly initialized tiny causal GPT-2 model was checked in FP32 and BF16 with FP32 logprobs for both loss methods. Excluded logprobs have zero direct policy gradient, and every model parameter gradient matches the existing sequence-token reference.

The additional regression scripts are retained locally and are not included in this production-only diff. These checks validate loss autograd and a small GPU model backward pass. They do not constitute a rollout-to-optimizer distributed training run; Megatron collectives are substituted in the local loss checks.

The follow-up checks found no additional changes needed in this two-file patch. I am keeping the PR as a draft for further review.

# Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue above, if there is one.
- [ ] I have reviewed and understand every changed line, and I can explain how the change works and why it is correct.
- [x] I have run the relevant tests or reproductions locally, and included the commands and results above (if applicable).
- [x] I am responsible for the content of this PR, regardless of how it was produced.

             seq_level_log_weights = ((log_ratio * completion_mask).sum(-1)
                                      / completion_mask.sum(-1).clamp(min=1.0)).unsqueeze(-1)

                 log_importance_weights = seq_level_log_weights

                 seq_level_log_weight = seq_level_log_weights.detach()
